name: README
rows: Immune recruitment signatures and cellular context in inflammatory neuropathies
v2.4.0; 2026-09-22; prepared update, not an already published release
Source data for all five main figures and seven supplementary figures in the current manuscript.
The exact numerical inputs or reported source estimates used for plotted points, intervals, heatmaps and counts.
FASTQ, CellBender matrices and original proteomics acquisitions remain at their public repositories. They are not recreated in this workbook.
A study-design schematic. Its table contains design labels and counts, not experimental measurements.
Blank cells mean unavailable or not applicable, not zero. Read each sheet with INDEX.
Figure 5 C/D contain anonymous score/INCAT pairs; no donor linkage across panels is implied by row order.
Preserve distinct q8, q80/q89 historical, q91 expanded, q9 new and q17 clinical families; they are not interchangeable.

Public quantitative exports and feasibility audit are included in the GitHub ZIP. Missing reliable sample-to-diagnosis mapping prevents independent nerve validation; this is not a negative validation result.
Run python current/analysis/reproduce_figures.py --out rebuilt_figures from the extracted repository root.
Project-derived tables and figures: CC BY 4.0. External source material retains original terms.

name: INDEX
rows: Schematic, not experimental measurements. CSF contrasts share participants.
Seven programmes in three cohorts; FDR retained from each cohort.
DerSimonian–Laird pooled effects with modified Hartung–Knapp intervals.
Pooled effects after each omitted cohort; these are sensitivity estimates, not additional cohorts.
Normal-approximation display intervals. Source P and q are kept separately.
Plotted fixed and random effects; normal-approximation intervals.
All 11 modified Hartung–Knapp intervals include zero; retain all pooling methods.
Intervals from normal approximation; colours reflect source q. Shared participants.
Intervals from normal approximation; colours reflect source q. Shared participants.
CIDP; thirteen genes in seven cell groups.
Diamonds use BH within cell group (eight modules). Expanded q91 supplied separately.
Relative representation among sampled nuclei; not absolute tissue cell abundance.
HC3 intervals. Adjustment for state composition attenuates the association.
Unadjusted primary P: Mann–Whitney. Display intervals: HC3. Adjusted P/q: HC3 family of nine. q89 is historical; q91 is the current expanded family.
Unadjusted primary P: Mann–Whitney. Display intervals: HC3. Adjusted P/q: HC3 family of nine. q89 is historical; q91 is the current expanded family.
Nine CIDP donors in pooled repair/damage Schwann cells. Row order does not identify or link donors across programmes.
Nine CIDP donors in pooled repair/damage Schwann cells. Row order does not identify or link donors across programmes.
Exact P enumerates all 9! assignments. Expanded q17 combines 15 original asymptotic P values with two new exact P values.
Donor-bootstrap expression intervals in 15 cell groups for four genes. Per-nucleus workflow without module eligibility threshold.
Published count; Wilson 95% interval. No individual biopsy observations are reconstructed.
Different endpoints from macrophage Fc expression; biological context, not replication of the Fc association.
HC3 intervals; q across eleven available genes.
Six prespecified displayed rows; donor/model sensitivities within the same cohort.
Three broad definitions and nine eligible refined subtypes; donor counts vary by annotation.
Dot colour = expression; area = 5 × percent. Zero detection is shown by a cross.
Odds ratio; MR beta; posterior probability
CDH4 association in women. MR estimates are copied from authoritative input rows, including GNG7 −2.11 and SLC39A3 −1.42.
CIDP minus CIAP in ten cell groups; no displayed contrast passes correction.
Original 15 asymptotic correlations and BH15; all q > 0.05.
Eleven genes × six preparations. Normal anatomical reference; no disease comparison.
80 original module tests + 9 programme extensions + 2 graft-reference contrasts.
Measured, variable genes used in each programme; missing genes are not imputed.
Public sequencing/count and normal BNB sources. Download separately for reanalysis.
